output.brief: The Kestria buffering problem is almost certainly caused by the new smart-TV app version 5.2, not by the CDN switch. Evidence: in session data for 12–25 October, all on Tessaline, smart-TV 5.2 stalls 5.9% of viewing time. Every other client is at 0.6–0.7%, including smart-TV 5.1 users, web and mobile. The pattern is the same on all three ISPs, so ISP congestion is ruled out. Stalls began 9 October, the day 5.2 went live. That is also when the cutover finished, which is why the CDN looked guilty. The handball launch came two days later and did not change the rate. I'm fairly confident (about 85%). Don't send the SLA notice, withhold fees or move traffic back, as that would not fix the problem. Don't mute the alert. Instead, revert 5.2's adaptive-streaming settings in Kestria and hold the wider rollout. Then add app-version breakdowns to the dashboard. Don't offer free months yet: the exit survey has no quality option, so the link between buffering and cancellations is unproven. The October price rise is a competing explanation. Check this by comparing cancellations of 5.2 users with other users.
